newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LG Semicon shares plunge on first day.
newsitem.headline: LG Semicon shares plunge on first day.

text.p: Shares of LG Semiconductor plunged 5.8 percent, or 1,900 won, to close at their daily limit of 30,800 won on their first day of trading on Saturday, brokers said.
"The stock plunged upon debuting on the market as investors were caught up with fears over the still sluggish semiconductor industry," said Yoo Nam-gil, researcher at Hyundai Securities.
The Korea Stock Exchange earlier set the stock's base price at 32,700 won per share, against the IPO subscription price of 20,000.
The base price was the weighted average of bids and offers received by the exchange.
LG Semicon, the world's seventh-biggest dynamic random access memory supplier, is 46.32 percent owned by LG Electronics Inc. Both firms are units of LG Group.
Share volume totalled 132,800 shares, with sell orders for a further 405,000 shares unmatched, brokers said.
"Many seemed to believe that earning 10,800 won per share is a good deal at this time when prospects for the semiconductor shares still remain gloomy," said an LG Securities broker.
He was referring to the gap between the stock's lower price limit of 30,800 won and its subscription price of 20,000 won.
Brokers said investors saw the stock's appropriate price level at 50 percent to 60 percent of the share price of Samsung Electronics, the world's largest DRAM chip seller.
